headline: High-risk data-engineering pair: Kestra can write/egress broadly, while awesome-selfhosted is a non-runnable knowledge list with no direct interaction surface.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No plausible prompt-injection bridge is documented. awesome-selfhosted is a non-runnable knowledge-management list with no I/O surfaces, while kestra is an orchestrator with file and network capabilities. Without a shared channel or evidence that either ingests the other’s outputs by default, the pathway is blocked.
conditions: IF a shared filesystem, clipboard, or message queue is introduced between the pair, reassess injection risk.
IF kestra is configured to parse content from awesome-selfhosted as executable instructions, the risk changes.
mitigations: Keep the pair disconnected from shared copy-paste workflows.
Do not pipe list content into kestra task definitions.
Use provenance labels on any imported text.
requires-engineering: add content-type separation between reference material and executable workflow inputs.

B_data_leakage.rationale: awesome-selfhosted touches no data classes and has no runtime I/O, while kestra can read/write files and egress broadly. There is no documented shared workspace or sensitive data class overlap, so leakage is limited unless an operator manually places secrets into kestra-managed files or inputs.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same filesystem path, leakage risk increases.
IF sensitive inputs are stored under /app/storage or /tmp for kestra to process, data exposure becomes plausible.
mitigations: Avoid storing secrets in kestra-accessible directories.
Separate reference docs from workflow storage.
Restrict kestra jobs from reading unrelated files.
Review any manual export from awesome-selfhosted before importing into kestra.
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation at the OS or container layer.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: awesome-selfhosted has no write or execution capability, but kestra can execute shells, spawn subprocesses, and write files. The pair does not show direct contention, yet kestra’s broad mutable access means conflicts can arise if both are pointed at the same directory or shared artifacts. Uncertainty about orchestration locking keeps this above low.
conditions: IF kestra instances write to the same directory without external locking, file conflicts are possible.
IF the pair is deployed against a shared git checkout or artifact store, concurrent mutation risk increases.
mitigations: Assign kestra a dedicated storage path.
Avoid shared git working trees.
Serialize writes with a lock file or queue.
Limit kestra to read-only access where possible.
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination for shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: awesome-selfhosted can act as a source of recommendations, and kestra can operationalize inputs into workflows, notifications, or external actions. If curated content from the list is treated as authoritative without verification, kestra may propagate bad assumptions into downstream tasks. The interaction is inferred, not directly documented, so uncertainty is escalated to medium.
conditions: IF kestra consumes list-derived recommendations as workflow parameters, cascading errors are possible.
IF downstream tasks send email, Slack, or cloud actions based on those parameters, impact expands.
mitigations: Require human review before turning recommendations into workflows.
Validate all imported fields against an allowlist.
Add a dry-run step before any external action.
Log provenance for every imported recommendation.
requires-engineering: implement schema validation between reference content and execution tasks.

E_compliance.rationale: No specific residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented for either agent. awesome-selfhosted is a static knowledge resource, while kestra handles logs, artifacts, and cloud-connected data; compliance risk only appears if regulated data is routed into kestra’s storage or external integrations. The other agent is not cited further because no compliance obligations are stated for it.
conditions: IF regulated data is processed through kestra storage or external APIs, compliance review is required.
IF retention settings on kestra artifacts exceed policy, a mismatch exists.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of kestra workflows.
Set short retention on logs and artifacts.
Disable unnecessary external integrations.
Document data residency for any cloud targets.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for retention and residency.
